clue.text: Associate party with stimulation

parts.note: a side is a party or faction in a dispute
a kick is a thrill or stimulation, as in getting a kick out of something

explanation.surface: Someone linking a celebration with excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or junior partner, so a synonym for an associate.

clue.text: No movement, but not against dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters are moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A paradox: standing still, though not opposed to dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a state of no flow or development, a complete lack of movement.

clue.text: American lady at first conscious, snatched by cleric

indicators.note: snatched by means grabbed and held, so the lady pieces go inside

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman

indicators.note: at first means take only the opening letter

parts.note: aware means conscious

explanation.surface: A woman, first alert, is kidnapped by a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A Delawarean is a person from Delaware, a US state, so an American.

clue.text: Danish rhino put up in Camden, or Kensington

indicators.note: put up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the London place names

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Danish rhinoceros housed in one of two London districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hiding place and 'put up' (upwards in a down clue) reverses ENORK. Rhino is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old slang for money, and the krone is the currency of Denmark.

clue.text: Coming together, but Ginger can't go mad

indicators.note: mad means wild and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: People assembling, though a red-haired friend is unable to attend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges GINGER CANT GO, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Congregating means gathering into a crowd or assembly.

clue.text: Drunk was collared by elderly assassin

indicators.note: being collared means being held round the neck, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: elderly means old

indicators.note: drunk describes the word was as reeling, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old killer, the worse for drink, was arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' and 'collared' both sound like an arrest story, but one scrambles and one encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Harvey Oswald was the man who shot President Kennedy in 1963, a famous assassin.

clue.text: Transport bound for moon? Small steps with it

parts.note: paces are steps
hip and with it both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: Echoes of the moon landing's small step.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceship is a vehicle for travelling in space, the kind that could carry people to the moon.

clue.text: 12 song from us: England Lay in Ruins

indicators.note: in ruins means wrecked and broken apart, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A New Year's Eve song whose words say England lies wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is NEW YEAR'S EVE; 'in Ruins' rearranges US ENGLAND LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Auld Lang Syne is the Robert Burns song traditionally sung at midnight on the last night of the year.

clue.text: Today's is 12: go out with people!

definitions.meaning: the ... today is 31 December, New Year's Eve
to go out with someone romantically

explanation.surface: It is New Year's Eve, so get out and socialise!
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is NEW YEAR'S EVE, which is a date on the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is a day on the calendar, and to date someone is to go out with them.

clue.text: A shout keeps two learners in comprehensive

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the learners are held inside the other letters

parts.note: a shout is British slang for one's turn to buy a round of drinks
L is the learner-driver plate letter; two of them give LL

explanation.surface: A cry from a driving instructor with two pupils on board.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'my shout' means it is my turn to buy the drinks, a round.
explanation.definitionFit: All-round means covering every aspect, a synonym of comprehensive, as in an all-round education.

clue.text: Striker satisfied quaffing a litre left

indicators.note: quaffing is drinking down, so the swallowed letters go inside

parts.note: to meet a demand is to satisfy it, so met means satisfied

explanation.surface: A footballer, content after downing a litre, has gone home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer, but it is a tool that strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A mallet is a hammer with a large head, a tool used for striking things.

clue.text: Conclude legal presentation on Jagger's condition?

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
Mick Jagger fronts the Rolling Stones, so his band is the Stones
a case is a state of affairs or condition

explanation.surface: A lawyer finishing, or a question about how Mick Jagger is.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer rests their case when they finish presenting evidence and argument.

clue.text: Hogmanay rave, Sweeney involved …

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Scottish year-end party with a Sweeney mixed up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges RAVE SWEENEY. The ellipsis runs the surface on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is the Scottish name for 31 December and its celebrations, the last night of the year.

clue.text: Musician Nick during riot mentioned participant

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to nick is to steal, and stealing during a riot is to loot
a player is a participant in a game

explanation.surface: A musician named Nick played a part in a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name; it is the verb to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lute player plays the lute, a stringed instrument, so is a musician.

clue.text: Couriers provided with pickle and mixed greens

parts.note: a pickle is a mess or predicament

indicators.note: mixed means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Delivery riders bringing chutney and a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Messengers carry messages or packages, which is what couriers do.

clue.text: … church on rocky outcrop set ablaze

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Continuing the party: a church on a hilltop goes up in flames.
explanation.definitionFit: To torch something is to set fire to it deliberately.

clue.text: School heads curse aloud Reveller's activities?

parts.note: high school heads, read as the word high that heads school in high school

indicators.note: aloud means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a jinx is a curse

explanation.surface: Head teachers swear; is that what a party animal gets up to?
explanation.walkthrough: Reveller is the setter's pseudonym, so the definition is a joke on the setter's own fun.
explanation.definitionFit: High jinks are boisterous fun and revelry, just what a reveller gets up to.

clue.text: Supped in good hotel by river lodge

indicators.note: in places the eating inside the good-hotel letters

parts.note: H is Hotel in the radio alphabet
to sup is to have supper, so supped means ate
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Someone dined at a fine hotel beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatehouse is a small building at the entrance to an estate, also called a lodge.

clue.text: Primate called to stop openly gay article

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so the calling letters plug the middle of the other word

parts.note: out means openly gay
rang means telephoned, called
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A phone call meant to block an openly gay article from publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' could be an archbishop, but here it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The orangutan is a great ape, one of the primates.

clue.text: Demand to squeeze juice from grapes?

definitions.meaning: to ... is to urge or demand, as in ... for an answer
a wine ... crushes grapes, and to ... them is to squeeze out the juice

explanation.surface: Insisting on making wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Press means both insist urgently and crush fruit to extract its liquid.

clue.text: Tomorrow's link holds place for blues legend

parts.note: the puzzle is set on New Year's Eve, so tomorrow is January: Jan is

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the place letters sit inside the link word

parts.note: to join is to link

explanation.surface: A note about the next day's connection to a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is New Year's Eve, so 'Tomorrow's' reads as 'Jan is', tomorrow being 1 January.
explanation.definitionFit: Janis Joplin was an American singer of the 1960s famed for her blues-rock voice.

clue.text: Constituent Oscar managed to guzzle gallon

parts.note: O is Oscar in the radio alphabet

indicators.note: to guzzle is to swallow greedily, so the gallon goes inside

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: An award-winner managed to drink a whole gallon.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a constituent part of a body or system, as in an organ of government.

clue.text: House arrests good for regret after 12?

indicators.note: arrests means holds in custody, so the good letter is held inside

parts.note: Hanover is a royal house that ruled Britain from 1714

explanation.surface: A household detains someone for good, to their regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is NEW YEAR'S EVE; the morning after brings its sore head.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is the sick feeling after heavy drinking, often regretted the morning after a party.

clue.text: See 22
Victor trapped in a depression finds Dawn

indicators.note: trapped in means caught inside, so V goes within the other letters

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
V is Victor in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A winner caught in a hollow finds a woman named Dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' looks like a name; it means a beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival or coming, the dawn of something new.

clue.text: See 7
Fish, fish not loud? On the contrary!

definitions.text: Fish, fish not loud? On the contrary!

parts.note: a gar is a long thin fish with a beaked snout

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the letter for loud out of the second fish

parts.note: taken as the word fish itself
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Is this fish quiet? Quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The question asks whether the result is 'not loud'; 'On the contrary!' says it is loud, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means gaudy and showy, and a loud colour or outfit is a garish one.

clue.text: Writer over Christmas is touring ancient city

indicators.note: over in a clue tells us to turn the word for Christmas over, back to front

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city
is gives its own letters, touring on after the city to finish the name

explanation.surface: An author spends the holiday visiting an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the definition, and the surface hides that the author's own name is split across Christmas and the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Uris was the American novelist who wrote Exodus.
